title: Performance Correlation Cafe — latency & throughput sync (Dec 5 2026)
content:
Purpose: quick informal sync to compare recent bench runs, surface cross-cutting signals (latency spikes that track with throughput knobs), and agree on a short hypothesis matrix to drive next week’s micro-runs.

Attendees: Priya, Evan, Leila, Tomás (+ async notes from SRE on alerting changes)

High-level summary:
- Observed a 12–18% p95 latency regression in mixed-seq smoke runs after the kernel selection change (kernel-v2) rolled to 40% traffic on the canary fleet on 2026-12-02.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) appears stable for steady-state long-seq jobs, but short-burst QPS profiles show increased queueing (queue depth bump from median 2 -> 6).
- KV-cache hit rate steady; however prefix cache eviction p99 correlated with larger request sizes (multi-turn chat with nested tool calls).
- Initial hypothesis: kernel-v2 improves single-token exec throughput backpressure but increases scheduler-induced head-of-line blocking for interleaved small requests.

What we ran since last sync: (short notes)
- Controlled A/B shadow run (same model, kernel-v1 vs kernel-v2) across identical instance types. 2k requests each, mixed seq distribution (10/50/256 tokens).
- Canary real-traffic capture (10m traces) with flamegraphs + sample KV cache telemetry.
- Warmup experiment: disabled continuous batching for 5% of canary nodes to compare micro-latency.
- Queue-depth sweep: synthetic generator ramping to 600 QPS for small-seq traffic to examine queue growth and tail latency.

Key observations (data snippets):
- A/B p50/p95: kernel-v1 p95=98ms -> kernel-v2 p95=115ms (mixed seq). p50 unchanged.
- Queue-depth sweep: median queue depth correlated with request size distribution; for small-seq heavy tails, queue depth p90 moved from 3 -> 9 under kernel-v2.
- Flamegraph samples show increased blocking in scheduler wait time slice labeled "batch_window_wait" for kernel-v2 nodes.
- KV cache: overall hit rate ~82% both sides; eviction spikes match a small subset of traces where tool-calls chain length >3.

Hypothesis matrix (quick):
H1: kernel-v2 increased scheduling window to favor larger batches — helps throughput but hurts small request tail latency.
H2: cache eviction patterns + interleaved tool calls lead to hot-key contention causing head-of-line stalls visible as queue depth spikes.
H3: Changes in default batching heuristic parameters (alpha/beta) deployed with kernel-v2 produce higher variance when request size distribution is multimodal.

Priority experiments to run (owner, target date):
- E1: Micro-canary with reduced batch_window_ms on kernel-v2 nodes (owner: Evan, due: 2026-12-08). Goal: see if lowering window shrinks p95 without dropping throughput beyond 3%. Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, batch size distribution.
- E2: Isolated heatmap on KV hotspots — run targeted traces that reproduce nested tool-calls and capture per-key lock/eviction rates (owner: Leila, due: 2026-12-09).
- E3: Synthetic workload that simulates mixed-seq interleaving (owner: Tomás, due: 2026-12-07). Compare observed queue growth against queue-theory model (M/G/1 approximation) to validate scheduler assumptions.
- E4: Canary with batching disabled for a small percentage to characterize best-case micro-latency for short requests (owner: Priya, due: 2026-12-08).

Measurements and acceptance criteria:
- If p95 on small-seq traffic drops to within 7% of kernel-v1 baseline while throughput loss <= 3% -> consider tuned kernel-v2 rollout with reduced batch_window.
- If kv-hotspot mitigation reduces eviction spike frequency by >=50% on nested-tool traces -> add hotspot-aware eviction rule to optimizer.

Open questions (from discussion):
- Are scheduler wait metrics instrumented at sufficient granularity? (SRE requested an extra histogram for batch_window_wait per core). Action: SRE to add metric (ticket PERF-1994).
- How much of the tail is client-side queuing vs runtime-side? Need trace-level client->runtime latency breakup. Action: add an extra client sampling header + correlate trace ids (owner: Tomás).
- Is there a realistic workload that mimics nested tool-call distribution? We have anecdotal customer traffic; need to synthesize representative generator. Action: Leila to draft generator config by 12/07.

Short-term mitigations we can deploy quickly:
- Temporary autoscale policy tweak: allow for faster burst capacity on specific canary nodes to reduce queue depth while we triage. (Ops has a rollback plan)
- Tune batch_window_ms from default 8ms -> 4ms for 10% of kernel-v2 nodes to measure impact.

Artifacts collected (links/notes):
- A/B run logs: s3://perf-archives/2026-12-05/ab-kernelv1-vs-v2-2k.tar.gz (internal)
- Flamegraph samples: gist:flame-2026-12-05 (internal)
- Synthetic generator config: GH:bench/generators/mixed-seq-config-2026-12-05.yaml

Action items (owners + due):
- Evan: run E1 micro-canary and post results + batch size histogram (due 12/08).
- Leila: implement kv-hotspot capture + share synthetic traces (due 12/09).
- Tomás: implement client sampling header + run synthetic interleaving test (due 12/07).
- Priya: coordinate quick autoscale tweak and track effects on queue depth (due 12/06, update at 12/06 18:00 PT).
- SRE: add per-core batch_window_wait histogram to telemetry (perf ticket PERF-1994, due 12/10).

Notes to follow-ups:
- Keep experiment runs small and reproducible (seeded RNG for generator). Save raw traces with trace ids that map to A/B buckets.
- For all canary changes, maintain immediate rollback toggles and a playbook entry with exact commands (copy current rollback section into the ticket).
- Try to capture 1 minute of full-resolution traces at the start of the canary window to get cold-cache behavior.

Meeting cadence:
- Quick sync same time next week (Dec 12) to review E1-E3 results. If regressions persist, escalate to perf-blitz working group with additional SRE attendance.

Appendix (quick diagnostic snippets):
- Command used for queue-depth generator: 
  ./bench-runner --profile mixed-seq --qps 600 --duration 300 --clients 120 --seed 42 --trace-ids out/trace-mixed-12-05.json

- Example trace excerpt (anonymized): 
  trace_id: 0000abcd | total_client_to_response_ms: 218 | runtime_processing_ms: 170 | queue_time_ms: 28 | kernel_exec_ms: 60 | batch_window_wait_ms: 52

- Quick checklist for reproducing experiment:
  1) Deploy kernel-v2 flags to a 10-node canary pool
  2) Enable tracing with sample rate 100% for 60s
  3) Run bench-runner (seeded) against canary pool and collect traces
  4) Upload artifacts to s3 and link in ticket

If you have additional data (especially customer traces that hit nested-tool chains), drop them into the PERF-1987 ticket and tag the owners. We prioritized quick, small experiments this week rather than broad fleet rollouts.

End.
